# Copilot Prompt Repository: Best Practices

This repository is dedicated to storing and sharing high-quality AI prompts for use with GitHub Copilot and similar tools. Follow these guidelines to ensure clarity, effectiveness, and maintainability of your markdown prompt files.

## 1. Prompt Structure
- **Title:** Start each prompt with a clear, descriptive title as a top-level heading (`#`).
- **Purpose:** Briefly explain the intent and expected outcome of the prompt.
- **Instructions:** Use concise, direct language. Break complex instructions into numbered or bulleted lists.
- **Examples:** Provide input/output examples when possible to clarify expected behavior.
- **Formatting:** Use markdown features (headings, lists, code blocks) for readability.

## 2. Writing Effective Prompts
- **Be Specific:** Clearly state the task, constraints, and desired output format.
- **Avoid Ambiguity:** Use precise language. Define any domain-specific terms.
- **Limit Scope:** Focus each prompt on a single task or concept.
- **Test Prompts:** Validate prompts with Copilot to ensure they produce useful results.

## 3. File Organization
- **Naming:** Use descriptive filenames (e.g., `python-data-cleaning.md`, `react-component.md`).
- **Grouping:** Organize prompts by domain, language, or use case in subfolders if needed.
- **Versioning:** Update prompts as best practices evolve. Use changelogs or comments for major revisions.

## 4. Documentation & Metadata
- **Metadata Block:** Optionally include a metadata section at the top (author, tags, last updated).
- **References:** Link to related prompts or external resources for further reading.

## 5. Licensing & Attribution
- **Respect Copyright:** Only include prompts you have rights to share. Attribute sources when adapting content.
- **License:** Ensure the repository and prompts are covered by a clear, permissive license (e.g., MIT).

## 6. Community Contributions
- **Pull Requests:** Encourage improvements and new prompts via PRs. Review for clarity and usefulness.
- **Issues:** Use issues to discuss prompt improvements, bugs, or new ideas.

## 7. Accessibility & Inclusivity
- **Inclusive Language:** Avoid bias and stereotypes. Use gender-neutral and culturally sensitive language.
- **Accessibility:** Ensure prompts are readable and usable by a wide audience.

---

For more information, see [GitHub Copilot documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot) and [OpenAI prompt engineering guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-engineering).
